I didn't send the 0.5 ETH. Your other wallet looks compromised, and any ETH sent to it would probably be taken right away.

**What I found:**
- **`0x1eb07b01de209b53427fd348aed96d4b72c2ff62` isn't a plain wallet.** It has an EIP-7702 delegation, meaning it's been set to run the code of contract `0xef93688b67019e4b48f19d924f9f8c1f01fb4b3f`.
- **That contract acts as a "sweeper."** Its code sends the address's entire ETH balance to `0xc9dc9a3ce543a67b0990367dc8d9bb1d61991890` the moment any ETH arrives. That's the same transaction as your deposit, so you'd never get to use the ETH for gas.

Unless you set this delegation up yourself and know both of those addresses, this is the usual setup for a drained wallet. Attackers who have a wallet's private key sweep any ETH sent to it so the owner can't pay gas to rescue the tokens still inside.

**What I'd suggest:**
1. Treat that wallet's private key or seed phrase as compromised. Don't send it any more ETH.
2. If tokens are still stuck in it, use a private-bundle rescue tool, such as a Flashbots-based "rescue" service. It pays gas and moves the tokens out in a single bundle, so the sweeper never gets a chance to grab the ETH.
3. Check that the wallet you're using now (`0xa73b…9a9a`) hasn't also been exposed, for example through a shared seed phrase or the same malicious site or signature.

If you did set up this delegation on purpose and recognize `0xc9dc…1890` as yours, tell me and I'll reconsider. Otherwise I'd strongly advise against sending.
